purpose: A census of the `paper`-prefixed declaration names in DavisKahan, and a mechanically applicable rename proposal. Nothing here has been applied. The intent is that a reviewer accepts or amends this document, and the rename is then a mechanical application of `renames[].current -> renames[].proposed` rather than a judgement call taken 238 times.
motivation: The 2026-09-01 rename replaced `PaperUnitaryInvariantNorm` with `SymmetricNormingFunction` because the name recorded provenance where the mathematics had its own name. That decision was never generalised, and `paper` is not in the naming classification's banned-token list, so the rest of the family was left in place. Measured here: of the declarations carrying the token, the great majority contrast with nothing -- there is no other `blockCompression`, `diagonalPair`, or `projectorDifference` in the tree -- so the prefix distinguishes nothing and reads as unfinished. ForTauCeti, the permanent product, already carries none of these names.

policy.provenance_only: The token distinguishes nothing: no declaration of the stripped name exists. Proposed action is to drop the prefix. These are mechanical.
policy.contrastive_decision_required: A declaration of the stripped name already exists, so the prefix currently carries meaning. Each of these needs a human decision -- which spelling is canonical, and what the other becomes -- and MUST NOT be renamed mechanically.
policy.dependent_declaration_names: Declarations whose own names begin with the renamed one. They have to move in the same commit, or a lemma stops matching the object it is about.
policy.not_covered: Prose. Docstrings and audit narratives say 'the paper's ...' in the ordinary English sense, which is correct and stays. Only declaration names are proposed here.

application_notes: Statement pins under `.leanq/` regenerate; they are not edited by hand.

`Challenge/**` and `comparator/*.json` hold declaration names as data and are not compiled by a default build. Run `python3 scripts/check_declaration_name_drift.py` and `lake build Challenge` after applying.
`Audits/ResultSemanticSurface.lean` names every canonical declaration; the result-inventory checker rejects a canonical declaration missing from it.

Re-pin statements and re-stamp `semantic_review_sweep.canonical_evidence_sha256` from the post-rename data, and record in the inventory review that the change is rename-only, with the evidence for that claim.

renames.note: Depends on the hilbert-schmidt family decision: if the duplicate concept is deleted, this theorem is restated against the canonical ForTauCeti API rather than renamed.

verification.proposal_internal_collisions_note: No two proposed names coincide, so applying the map cannot merge two distinct declarations.
verification.mathlib_short_name_collisions_note: No proposed short name also names a Mathlib declaration. Checked by scanning every declaration head under `.lake/packages/mathlib/Mathlib`. This is the hazard that would bite hardest -- `hilbertSchmidtNorm` and `projectionBlock` are the kind of name Mathlib might already own -- and it is clear.
fortauceti_references: ForTauCeti/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/SchattenNorm.lean:375 -- a docstring naming `paperHilbertSchmidtNorm_eq_rectangularFrobenius`. ForTauCeti declares none of these names; this is a prose cross-reference into DavisKahan and must be updated with the rename.
verification.method: Declaration heads parsed from every .lean file under DavisKahan/ and ForTauCeti/; occurrence counts are word-boundary matches per surface. Counts are evidence of blast radius, not a substitute for applying the rename and rebuilding.
verification.angle_family_finding: Checked directly, 2026-09-02. The `paper*` angle operators are the functional calculus of the angle: `paperCosAngleOperatorC = cfc Real.cos (paperAngleOperatorC U V)`, and similarly for sin, tan, sin 2, tan 2. The existing UNPREFIXED names are different constructions built on the directed sine: `cosAngleOperatorC = modulus (P_V ∘L P_U)`, `sinTwoAngleOperatorC = 2 • (sinAngleOperatorDirectedC * cosAngleOperatorC)`, and `tanAngleOperatorC` composes `sinAngleOperatorDirectedC` with an inverse cosine equivalence and additionally takes an acuteness hypothesis. So the unqualified names currently denote the directed objects while the canonical functional-calculus objects carry a provenance prefix. That is the inconsistency the collision exposed, and it is why the resolution is to normalise the family rather than rename around it.
verification.cited_names_present: All 52 declarations named in the amended families were confirmed to exist in the tree before being written here.
verification.embedded_token_note: Checked after amendment: no proposed name contains the token, as a prefix or embedded. The mechanical pass left nine half-converted, which is worse than either endpoint -- the name would no longer match the object it is about. Each is now renamed by applying the family decision to every object it mentions.

not_yet_decided: Whether to apply any of this, and when relative to the hostile-review sign-off. Nothing is applied.

The angle-family normalisation moves EXISTING unprefixed declarations, so it is a two-sided rename and cannot be applied by the mechanical map alone; it needs its own pass with a build after each family.
Whether the Hilbert--Schmidt and plane consolidations happen as part of this campaign or as separate migrations, since they delete concepts rather than rename them.
policy_statement: Provenance goes in namespaces, modules, docstrings, and source-census metadata. A permanent declaration name describes the mathematical object, or the representation that distinguishes it from another object. Resolving a collision is therefore never a matter of finding a different prefix: where two names collide, the collision is usually exposing an API distinction that should be settled.
amendment_note: Amended on hostile review of the first proposal. The mechanical pass stripped `paper` and stopped, which would have preserved several latent defects under new spellings: it left the DIRECTED angle constructions holding the unqualified names, produced `source*` names that are still provenance, left `paper` embedded mid-name in theorem names whose prefix alone was stripped, and proposed competing for names the canonical ForTauCeti API already owns. The families below replace the mechanical proposal wherever they overlap it.

families.title: Canonical angle-function objects take the unqualified names; the directed constructions say `directed`.
families.rationale: The unqualified names currently hold the directed/product constructions while the canonical functional-calculus objects carry a provenance prefix. Swapping them gives a predictable API -- angleOperatorC, sinAngleOperatorC, cosAngleOperatorC, tanAngleOperatorC, sinTwoAngleOperatorC, tanTwoAngleOperatorC and their directed* siblings -- and puts the qualifier on the construction that is genuinely special. This is a two-sided rename: several EXISTING unprefixed declarations move, so it cannot be applied by stripping prefixes.

families.title: Consolidate into the canonical ForTauCeti API rather than renaming.
families.rationale: `ContinuousLinearMap.IsHilbertSchmidt`, `hilbertSchmidtEnergy` and `hilbertSchmidtENorm` already exist and are canonical, and the repository has already proved that the source-side approximation-singular-value definitions describe the same notion. Renaming the paper copies into those names would compete with the canonical API; the polished end state migrates consumers to it and deletes the duplicate concept, keeping the mathematics as characterisation theorems. Any intermediate that must survive the migration is named for what distinguishes it, `singularValueHilbertSchmidtEnergy` / `singularValueHilbertSchmidtNorm`, not for the canonical name.

moves.fallback: singularValueHilbertSchmidtNorm, only if an intermediate is needed during migration

families.title: One canonical name for the two-dimensional model space.
families.rationale: `Plane` is too generic to be a reusable name and the aliases add nothing. One name, `PlanarModelSpace 𝕜` for `EuclideanSpace 𝕜 (Fin 2)`, used as `PlanarModelSpace ℝ` and `PlanarModelSpace ℂ`. Role-bearing model names replace `planeE0`-style names.

families.title: Name the extra data, not its provenance.
families.rationale: These wrappers are not the canonical problem structures under another name: they carry additional data, a chosen `SinThetaRepresentative`. `RepresentativeProblem` says why a second structure exists; `Paper...Problem` does not.

families.title: `Block`, `Modulus`, `GraphCoordinate`, `SelectedBranch` carry the real distinction.
families.rationale: Stripping `paper` from the `paperSource*` family leaves `source*`, which is the same provenance problem in a different word. These objects live on source-coordinate block spaces, so `Block` is the information worth keeping, and the positive U -> U modulus objects should visibly say `Modulus`.

families.title: Names record mathematical scope, not review verdicts.
families.rationale: `faithful` is review terminology. The discriminator these theorems actually carry is the selected branch, so the name should say that. `paperTanTwoThetaRepresentative` is specifically a graph-coordinate operator and should say so rather than being stripped to a generic `Representative`.

moves.alternative: tanTwoTheta_orderedFormGap_symmetricNorming, if the ordered form gap is the stronger discriminator

families.title: Theorem names carrying the token mid-name are renamed in full.
families.rationale: Stripping only a leading prefix leaves names like `sineModulus_sq_add_paperCosineModulus_sq`, which is worse than either endpoint: half-converted, and now inconsistent with the object it is about. Each is renamed by applying the family decision to every object the name mentions.
